title: feat(desktop): exports keep the face above the zoom, even over a still screen (NIW2-575)
body:
PR 5 of the webcam-track stack ([#437 design](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/437) → [#441 recorder](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/441) → [#442 vault](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/442) → [#443 scene](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/443) → [#444 preview](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/444) → this). Linear [NIW2-575](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-575), parent [NIW2-565](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-565). Base: `feature/niw2-574-webcam-preview`.

## What this does

MP4 and GIF exports now draw the webcam layer the preview shows. The bubble stays in its corner above the zoomed screen, at its size, shape and mirror, and hides over hidden ranges. Both exports go through the one shared output composer. The webcam is the last thing drawn: after redactions, overlays, the zoom crop, and the Vertical/Square framing. Recordings without a webcam export exactly as before, with no extra decoding and the same "already exported" reuse.

## Why

With #441–#444 the face is its own layer, but an export would leave it out. This PR closes that gap.

## What changes for you

- **Exports of camera-on recordings include the face, above the zoom.**
- **The face keeps moving over a still screen.** Screen capture only produces frames when something on screen changes, so the export adds frames at the webcam's rate (30 fps) where the screen is still. Without them, the face would freeze for seconds over a slide.
- **A broken webcam file never breaks an export.** The export finishes without the layer and the error goes to Sentry. A missing file already behaved this way.
- **Exports of camera-on recordings made before this PR are never reused.** Their fingerprint now carries a `wc1` tag. Every other recording keeps its fingerprint, so its exports stay reusable.
- **On Vertical, a bubble never gets wider than the frame's shorter side.** The preview uses the same geometry, so the two stay in agreement.
- Share does not compose the webcam yet; that is #6 (NIW2-576).

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/export-worker.ts:341`: the fill loop.** Fills re-compose the held screen frame with the next webcam frame. Each declares its duration up to the next screen frame or the clip end; mediabunny overwrites every duration except the last. Fills stay inside their clip. They rely on the screen decoder's two-canvas pool keeping the previous frame for one more pull, which is documented in `canvas-sink-options.ts`. Decide whether that dependency on mediabunny 1.61 internals is acceptable.
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/compose-output-frame.ts:86`: the framer moved into `createOutputComposer`.** The order is frame → redactions → overlays → crop → framer → webcam. For exports without a webcam, the reviewer checked that the parameters and order are unchanged; look for anything that drifted.
3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/webcam-lockstep.ts:48`: `webcamLookupTime`.** It clamps the lookup to the clip's start, because the frame spanning a cut can start before it. The webcam frame, its layout and the camera scale all use that one time.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/export-reuse.ts:47`: the `wc1` tag sits in the edit fingerprint, not in `ENCODE_REVISION`.** An earlier version bumped `ENCODE_REVISION` on every preset, which would have re-encoded every export of every recording. Review E4 narrowed it.
5. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/webcam-source.ts:100`: `openWebcamSourceOrNone`.** It degrades to no layer on open or decode failures and reports the error once through a `webcam-error` worker message.

**Safe to skim:** `export-messages.ts`, `gif-messages.ts` and the plan type (pass-through), `webcam-fetch.ts`, `compose-webcam.ts` (drawing order: shadow → clip → mirror → image; tested), and the test files.

## Proof

| Criterion (NIW2-575) | What was done | How to check it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The worker decodes the webcam in lockstep (hold-last-frame) and draws it in the shared composer after the crop and the framer | Second Input; `webcam-lockstep.ts`; the composer draws the webcam last | `webcam-lockstep.test.ts` (30 vs 60/30 fps, offset, before first and after last frame, cut, pause); `compose-output-frame.test.ts` (order: webcam last, after the framer) | Unit tests pass |
| Vertical (Fill) and Square (Fit) keep the whole bubble inside the output | `webcamRect` caps at the shorter side; clamps inside | `compose-webcam.test.ts`: all 9 presets on Vertical and Square at the largest size | Unit tests pass |
| GIF shows the same layer as MP4 | Both workers use `createOutputComposer` with `plan.webcam` | `compose-output-frame.test.ts` (source-level check, weak: E7) and `use-gif-export.test.ts` | Unit tests pass. **Real GIF: not verified** |
| Recordings without a webcam keep their export behavior | No fetch, no second Input; the composer draws the old frame; fingerprint unchanged | `export-runner.test.ts`, `webcam-source.test.ts`, `export-reuse.test.ts` (pinned `edit:2bdufz02r20`) | Unit tests pass |
| Pure, worker-safe geometry, tested | `webcam-layout.ts`, `compose-webcam.ts`, `webcam-lockstep.ts` import only pure modules | Reviewer and Codex checked the imports | Unit tests pass |
| check-types, lint and tests pass | — | `vitest run`; pre-push `verify:local` | exit 0, 324 files, 3268 tests; pre-push passed |
| (Review) The face does not freeze over a still screen, and the timeline is not cut short | `webcamFillTimes`, `fillWebcamGap`, durations up to the next frame or clip end | `webcam-lockstep.test.ts` (3 s gap → 89 fills; hidden/ended/failed mid final gap reaches the end) | Unit tests pass; Codex re-ran an in-memory mediabunny mux: the 10 s track now ends at 10 s (it ended at 5.033 s before the fix) |

## Decisions

- **Fill frames at webcam cadence over still screens** (review E2). Options: accept a frozen face, re-encode the screen at a fixed rate, or fill only where the face changes. Taken: fill only where the face changes. That is the least extra work, and fills stop while the layer is hidden.
- **During a fill, the zoom crop stays at the held frame's span**, which keeps the redactions exact. The bubble's shrink scale follows the camera at the fill time, so during a zoom transition over a still screen the two can differ slightly (E9, follow-up).
- **Invalidate only camera-on exports, via a `wc1` tag in the edit fingerprint** (E4), not `ENCODE_REVISION`.
- **A broken webcam file degrades to no layer** (E3), the same as a missing one, and is reported to Sentry.
- **GIF reads webcam frames by random access** at each sampled time, because GIF samples sparse slots.
- **The webcam is decoded at its native size** (720p, or more with framing), so a zoomed framing stays sharp.
- **The bubble is capped at the frame's shorter side**, so a large bubble fits on Vertical. Size is still a fraction of output height, so bubbles look big on Vertical; changing that is a design call.

Rounds: 2 with Opus 5.5 (fresh-context reviewer) and 2 with Codex (cross-provider: CHANGES C1, then APPROVE with the reproduction re-run). Budget 5.
**Verdict for f4c162b1 (patch-id b5ad0a5d357f): approved, only nits remain.** (Opus re-checked 77ec29f2 and f4c162b1, the PR-bot fixes; E11, a latent TDZ if fetch ever threw synchronously, is a follow-up.)

## Checks

- `cd apps/kaipu-record && vitest run`: exit 0, 324 files, 3268 tests passed (on 77ec29f2).
- Pre-push `verify:local` (lint, oxfmt, build, check-types): passed on push.

## Manual verification

This is owner QA; agents do not run Electron on the owner's machine. You need a camera-on take from #441 or later.

**Setup:** `git checkout feature/niw2-575-webcam-export && bun install && bun run dev`, then open that recording in the editor.

**1. The face survives a zoom in the export** (the goal of the whole stack)
- Make sure an auto-zoom is on and export an MP4 (Balanced).
- Expect: in the exported file, the bubble stays in its corner above the zoom, and matches the preview frame for frame.
- Broken if: there is no face, the face zooms with the screen, or it sits in a different place than in the preview.
- Note: until #6, the old bubble is also burned into the screen pixels.

**2. A still screen**
- Record 15 s talking over a static slide, then export.
- Expect: your face moves the whole time.
- Broken if: the face freezes while the audio plays.

**3. Vertical and Square**
- Export Vertical (Fill) and Square (Fit) with the bubble in a corner, then at the largest size.
- Expect: the whole bubble is inside the frame.

**4. GIF**
- Export a GIF of the same range.
- Expect: the same bubble as the MP4.

**5. Hidden range**
- Hide the webcam over a range and export.
- Expect: no bubble in that range, and the video plays to its full length.

**6. An old recording**
- Export one made before #441.
- Expect: the export is the same as before, and "already exported" files are still reused.

## What I did not verify

- A real H.264 or GIF export with a webcam, and whether it matches the preview pixel for pixel. The shadow is an approximation.
- The fill loop end to end on a real still-screen recording; the pure helpers and Codex's in-memory mux are covered.
- Windows.
